To process large graphs efficiently using Gambit CLI and handle memory constraints, you can stream data and write results incrementally. For example, if running a command like `gambt degree input.graph > degrees.txt`, use Ruby to append output in chunks:

```ruby
# Open the output file for appending
File.open('degrees.txt', 'a') do |file|
  # Read the graph line by line (if processing live data)
  until EOF.not?
    file.write(chomp(gets))
    # Process each node's degree here, then write to file in batches
    sleep(0.1) # Simulate delay if needed
  end
end
```

If writing a large file programmatically:
```ruby
# Write parts of the file incrementally
(1..10000).each_slice(1000) do |i|
  chunk = "Node #{i.offset_while.not_nil? ? (i.offset_while.to_s : '-').to_s} - #{i.max.to_i} degree, Count: #{i.size}\n"
  write_file('output_part-#{i.object_id}.dat', true, chunk)
end
```

This approach ensures you don’t load the entire output into memory at once. Adjust based on your specific Gambit task and data flow.
